public_rationale: The advertised $199 price reasonably rounds to $200, and Rabbit confirms customers had begun receiving devices. The Verge, WIRED, and Engadget published clearly unfavorable completed reviews before May 6. More favorable initial impressions existed, so the evidence supports generally poor launch reviews rather than unanimous criticism.
limitations: This is a comparison of prominent launch reviews, not an exhaustive review census.
It does not assess later software improvements or later reviews.

public_payload.normalized_proposition: The $200 Rabbit R1 AI device has started shipping and its reviews are not good.

statement.excerpt: The device — which costs $200 — has already started shipping and the reviews are not good.

our_interpretation: $200 is ordinary rounding of a $199 advertised price.
Started shipping means customer distribution had begun, not that every preorder had shipped.
Reviews are not good means the overall verdicts of prominent launch reviews were generally unfavorable, not that every feature or early impression was negative.
Use the latest launch-review and delivery period, April through publication, for this ongoing observation.
A retail product price is not a claim about company revenue, spending, or valuation; metric_scope is therefore null.
criteria.support_condition: The R1 cost approximately US$200, customer deliveries had begun by publication, and several prominent completed launch reviews gave unfavorable overall verdicts.
criteria.contradiction_condition: The advertised price materially differed, customer distribution had not begun, or the prominent completed launch reviews were generally favorable.
